# CLAUDE.md - Testing Guide for OrcaSlicer

This guide provides comprehensive instructions for Claude Code when writing, maintaining, and understanding tests in the OrcaSlicer codebase.

## ⚠️ CRITICAL RULES - MUST FOLLOW

### 1. **SECTIONS IN LOOPS - NEVER REUSE NAMES**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause unpredictable behavior
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Bad loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        SECTION("Same name") {  // WRONG! Same name used multiple times
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use DYNAMIC_SECTION or incorporate counter
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Good loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        DYNAMIC_SECTION("Section " << i) {  // Unique name per iteration
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. **THREAD SAFETY - ASSERTIONS ARE NOT THREAD-SAFE**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([]() {
            REQUIRE(some_calculation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
        });
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Synchronize results, test on main thread
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    std::atomic<int> passed{0};
    
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([&passed]() {
            if (some_calculation() == expected) {
                passed++;
            }
        });
    }
    
    for (auto& t : threads) t.join();
    REQUIRE(passed == 4);  // Test results on main thread
}
```

### 3. **EXPRESSION DECOMPOSITION - AVOID BINARY OPERATORS**
❌ **WRONG**: Cannot decompose properly
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0 && b < 10);  // Shows "false" on failure, not individual values
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Split into separate assertions
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0);
REQUIRE(b < 10);  // Each shows individual values on failure
```

### 4. **FLOATING POINT - NEVER USE APPROX**
❌ **WRONG**: Approx is deprecated and asymmetric
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_value == Catch::Approx(expected));  // Deprecated!
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use floating point matchers
```cpp
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));     // 4 ULPs apart
```

### 5. **TEST ORDERING - ALWAYS USE RANDOM ORDER**
✅ **REQUIRED**: For CI/CD and development
```bash
# Essential flags for running tests
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# For test sharding (parallel execution), share random seed
./tests --order rand --shard-index 0 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 1 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 2 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
```

## Overview of OrcaSlicer's Testing Framework

OrcaSlicer uses **Catch2 v3** (currently v3.11.0, vendored in `tests/catch2/`) as its primary testing framework. The test suite is organized into several modules that mirror the project's architectural components:

> **Note**: Test files include the framework via `#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>` (the v3 single-header convenience include). All v3 features described in this guide are available.

### Test Structure
```
tests/
├── CMakeLists.txt              # Main test configuration
├── catch_main.hpp              # Custom test reporter
├── libslic3r/                  # Core library tests (21 test files)
├── fff_print/                  # FFF printing tests (12 test files)
├── sla_print/                  # SLA printing tests (4 test files)
├── libnest2d/                  # 2D nesting tests
├── slic3rutils/               # Utility tests
├── data/                      # Test data files and meshes
└── catch2/                    # Catch2 framework files
```

### Build Integration
- Tests are built using CMake with `catch_discover_tests()` integration
- Each test module creates a separate executable (e.g., `libslic3r_tests`, `fff_print_tests`)
- Test data directory is available via `TEST_DATA_DIR` preprocessor definition
- Custom verbose console reporter provides detailed test output

## Catch2 Features Guide

### Basic Assertions
```cpp
// Primary assertions - stop test on failure
REQUIRE(expression);
REQUIRE_FALSE(expression);

// Continuing assertions - continue test after failure  
CHECK(expression);
CHECK_FALSE(expression);

// Non-failing checks - record result but don't fail test
CHECK_NOFAIL(expression);  // Useful for assumptions that might be violated
```

### Exception Testing
```cpp
// Verify no exception is thrown
REQUIRE_NOTHROW(function_call());

// Verify any exception is thrown
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());

// Verify specific exception type
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(function_call(), SpecificException);

// Verify exception message
REQUIRE_THROWS_WITH(function_call(), "Expected error message");

// Verify exception with matchers (for partial matching)
REQUIRE_THROWS_MATCHES(function_call(), SpecificException, 
                       Catch::Matchers::Message("contains this"));
```

### Complex Assertions with Matchers
```cpp
#include <catch2/matchers/catch_matchers.hpp>

// String matchers
using Catch::Matchers::StartsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::EndsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::ContainsSubstring;
using Catch::Matchers::Equals;
using Catch::Matchers::Matches;  // Regex matching

REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, StartsWith("Expected prefix"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, ContainsSubstring("middle part"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, Matches(".*pattern.*"));

// Floating point matchers - ALWAYS use these instead of Approx!
using Catch::Matchers::WithinAbs;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinRel;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinULP;

REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));     // Absolute tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));      // Relative tolerance (1%)
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));         // ULP difference (requires IEEE-754)

// Combining matchers
REQUIRE_THAT(value, WithinRel(expected, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));
```

### BDD-Style Tests
Use for complex scenarios and user story testing:

> **Note**: BDD macros are aliases for TEST_CASE and SECTION with prefixed names
```cpp

    GIVEN("A specific setup condition") {
        GCodeWriter writer;
        // Setup code
        
        WHEN("User performs action") {
            auto result = writer.some_operation();
            
            THEN("Expected outcome occurs") {
                REQUIRE(result.size() > 0);
                
                AND_WHEN("Follow-up action occurs") {
                    auto next_result = writer.next_operation();
                    
                    THEN("Final outcome is correct") {
                        REQUIRE(next_result == expected);
```
```cpp
                    }
```
```cpp
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

## Running and Debugging Tests

### Running Tests

#### Essential Test Execution Patterns
```bash
# REQUIRED: Random order with assertion warnings (best practice)
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions
```

## Common Pitfalls and Solutions

### Floating-Point Comparisons

> **CRITICAL**: Never use Approx - it's deprecated due to asymmetry and other issues

❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == expected_volume);           // Exact equality
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == Catch::Approx(expected));   // Deprecated! Asymmetric!
```

✅ **Correct**: Always use floating point matchers
```cpp
// Absolute tolerance - good when values are near zero
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinAbs(expected_volume, 0.001));

// Relative tolerance - good for values with different magnitudes
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance

// ULP (Units in Last Place) - most precise, requires IEEE-754
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinULP(expected_volume, 4));

// Combined approach - relative OR absolute
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, 
    WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));

// Precision control for output
Catch::StringMaker<double>::precision = 15;  // Show more decimal places
```

### Why Approx is Problematic:
- **Asymmetric**: `Approx(10).epsilon(0.1) != 11.1` but `Approx(11.1).epsilon(0.1) == 10`
- **Double-only**: All computation done in `double`, causes issues with `float` inputs  
- **Default behavior**: Only uses relative comparison, so `Approx(0) == X` only works for `X == 0`

### Path Handling
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
std::string path = TEST_DATA_DIR + "/model.obj";  // May have path separator issues
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
std::string path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/model.obj";
// or use boost::filesystem for complex path operations
```

### Exception Testing
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
bool threw_exception = false;
try {
    risky_function();
} catch (...) {
    threw_exception = true;
}
REQUIRE(threw_exception);
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());
// or for specific exceptions
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(risky_function(), SpecificException);
```

### Thread Safety

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: Catch2 assertions are **NOT thread-safe** by default!

> **Note**: Catch2 v3.9.0+ has opt-in thread-safe assertions via `CATCH_CONFIG_EXPERIMENTAL_THREAD_SAFE_ASSERTIONS`. OrcaSlicer is on v3.11.0 but does not enable this flag, so assertions remain non-thread-safe by default.

❌ **Incorrect**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
std::thread t([&]() {
    REQUIRE(threaded_operation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
    CHECK(other_operation());                   // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
});
```

✅ **Correct**: Collect results, assert on main thread
```cpp
std::atomic<bool> success{false};
std::atomic<int> error_count{0};

std::thread t([&]() {
    // Do work in thread, collect results
    bool result1 = (threaded_operation() == expected);
    bool result2 = other_operation();
    
    if (result1 && result2) {
        success = true;
    } else {
        error_count++;
    }
});

t.join();

// Assert results on main thread
REQUIRE(success);
REQUIRE(error_count == 0);
```

#### Thread Safety Rules:
- **REQUIRE family**: Would terminate process in spawned threads (throws exception with no try-catch)
- **CHECK family**: Not thread-safe, can corrupt internal state
- **SKIP, FAIL, SUCCEED**: Not thread-safe even with v3 thread-safe assertions
- **Message macros**: INFO, CAPTURE, WARN - not thread-safe
- **STATIC_REQUIRE/CHECK**: Not thread-safe (relies on runtime registration)

### Memory Management
Use RAII and smart pointers in tests:
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Resource management", "[Memory]") {
    auto model = std::make_unique<Model>();
    // Automatic cleanup on test completion/failure
    
    REQUIRE(model->objects.empty());
}
```

## Performance Considerations

### Compilation Optimizations
```cpp
// In CMakeLists.txt or as preprocessor definition
#define CATCH_CONFIG_FAST_COMPILE  // 20% faster compilation, disables some features

// For faster test iteration during development

```

### Runtime Performance
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Performance-sensitive test", "[Performance]") {
    // Manual timing example (Catch2's built-in BENCHMARK macro is also available)
    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    
    auto result = expensive_operation();
    
    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);
    
    REQUIRE(result.is_valid());
    REQUIRE(duration.count() < 1000);  // Should complete in < 1 second
    
    INFO("Operation took " << duration.count() << "ms");
}
```

### Memory Leak Detection
```cpp
// For Windows builds - detects memory leaks

```

### Adding New Test Files
1. Create test file: `test_new_feature.cpp`
2. Add to appropriate `CMakeLists.txt`:

```cmake
# Basic test discovery
catch_discover_tests(${_TEST_NAME}_tests TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}: ")

# Advanced test discovery with customization
catch_discover_tests(${_TEST_NAME}_tests
    TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}: "
```

## Known Issues and Workarounds

### Platform-Specific Issues
```cpp
// MinGW/CygWin slow linking workaround
// Use: -fuse-ld=lld flag to speed up linking significantly

// Visual Studio 2017 raw string literal bug
#define CATCH_CONFIG_DISABLE_STRINGIFICATION
// This disables expression stringification but works around the compiler bug

// Visual Studio 2022 spaceship operator issue
// REQUIRE((a <=> b) == 0);  // May not compile with MSVC
// Workaround: use clang-cl or avoid spaceship in assertions

// QNX/VxWorks C stdlib issues
#include <cfoo>           // Use C++ headers
std::foo_function();     // Always call qualified
// NOT: #include <foo.h> and foo_function();
```

### Catch2 v3 Features Available

1. **1:1 correspondence**: One test binary per library/module

content.text:
I filled in the branding page and saved it, and I added the JusPrin staging sign-in address to the Google sign-in client Obico uses. The app still needs one click on "Publish app" from you. Until then, Google's own Audience page says only listed test users can sign in. Obico production signs in with this same client, so Google sign-in on app.obico.io may be failing for everyone right now. I haven't tested whether it is.

**Saved on the branding page** (elegoo-backend project):
- App name "Obico", support and developer contact email k@obico.io.
- Home page `https://www.obico.io/`, privacy policy `https://www.obico.io/privacy.html`, terms `https://www.obico.io/terms.html`. I checked that all three pages load.
- Authorized domains `obico.io` and `thespaghettidetective.com`. The client's existing sign-in addresses are on those two domains, plus localhost.
- I left the logo empty. Google says uploading one means submitting the published app for verification.

**Saved on the OAuth client** (the one ending `…ubm4silcbif4sgsc6qpfuc91403s04o2`): `https://jusprin-stg.obico.io/accounts/google/login/callback/` is now an authorized redirect address. I reloaded the page and it's there. Google says changes can take from 5 minutes to a few hours to apply.

**Why I couldn't publish:** clicking "Publish app" was blocked as a permission change I can't make for you. Your Chrome tab is open on the Audience page. Click "Publish app" and confirm. The status should change from "Testing" to "In production". Google may show a warning about verification. Basic sign-in only asks for email and profile, which usually doesn't need verification, but I haven't confirmed that for this project.

**Still waiting on you for staging:** the Namecheap tab wants the device verification code sent to your email. Once you've entered it, I'll add the `jusprin-stg` → `34.95.90.112` DNS record. Then I'll check the certificate, the site and Google sign-in on jusprin-stg.obico.io.

content.text:
JusPrin staging is up at https://jusprin-stg.obico.io. Google's certificate turned Active sometime between 15:59 and 17:35, and the login page now loads over normal HTTPS with a 200.

**What I checked in your Chrome:**
- The login page shows the JusPrin logo and email and password fields, and "Continue with Google" is the only social sign-in. There's no Apple button.
- Clicking "Continue with Google" opens Google's "Choose an account" page, which says "to continue to Obico". That means Google accepted the new jusprin-stg redirect address and the published consent screen. I stopped there, because picking an account would create a real JusPrin staging account under your Google identity. So the last step, Google sending you back and the server creating a JusPrin account, is untested. Email-code sign-in on staging was already confirmed earlier to create a separate JusPrin account.
- I closed both Chrome tabs I had opened, the Namecheap one and the Google Cloud one.

**One thing on the page is now wrong.** Under the JusPrin logo it says: "If you have an Obico account, you can use the same account to sign in here." Since JusPrin now keeps its own accounts, someone who follows that note gets a new, empty JusPrin account, not their Obico one. The sentence is in `backend/app/templates/account/login.html` line 34 in the obico-server repository. That repository is a submodule of tsd-enterprise, so fixing it means a commit there plus a submodule update in tsd-enterprise, which I'd leave for you to do. Since JusPrin is getting its own sign-in page later, you might be fine leaving the server's page alone until then.

**Still not done:**
- Production for jusprin.obico.io hasn't started: its certificate and ingress rule, the syndicate id sequence reset, the setup command, the DNS record and the Google redirect address.
- The ops branch `claude/jusprin-host` and the JusPrin branch `claude/elated-sutherland-84a741` are not pushed.

import re
import logging
from django.utils import translation
from django.conf import settings

from lib.syndicate import syndicate_from_request, settings_for_syndicate


RE_TSD_APP_PLATFORM = re.compile(r'TSDApp-(?P<platform>\w+)')

def additional_context_export(request):

    platform = request.GET.get('platform', None)      # Allow get parameter to override for debugging purpose
    if not platform:
        m = RE_TSD_APP_PLATFORM.match(request.headers.get('X-TSD-Platform', '') or request.headers.get('user-agent', ''))
        platform = m.groupdict()['platform'] if m else ''

    # TODO: JusPrin syndicate hack so that we can set branding without add a syndicate to the DB
    user_agent = request.META.get('HTTP_USER_AGENT', 'Not provided')
    if user_agent.startswith("JusPrin"):
        syndicate_name = 'jusprin'
    else:
        syndicate_name = syndicate_from_request(request).name

    syndicate_settings = settings_for_syndicate(syndicate_name)
    syndicate_settings['name'] = syndicate_name

    language = request.GET.get('lang') or request.META.get('HTTP_ACCEPT_LANGUAGE', 'en-US')


    return {
        'page_context': {
            'app_platform': platform,
            'syndicate': syndicate_settings,
            'language': language,
        }
    }


def additional_settings_export(request):
    settings_dict = {
        'TWILIO_COUNTRY_CODES': settings.TWILIO_COUNTRY_CODES,
    }

    return settings_dict

class EmailLookupBySyndicateTestCase(TestCase):
    """Every lookup of an account by address is allauth's own (EmailAddress
    rows, then User.email), kept to one syndicate."""

    def setUp(self):
        self.base, _ = Syndicate.objects.get_or_create(id=1, defaults={'name': 'base'})
        self.other, _ = Syndicate.objects.get_or_create(id=2, defaults={'name': 'yumi'})
        site, _ = Site.objects.get_or_create(domain='testserver', defaults={'name': 'testserver'})
        self.base.sites.add(site)
        site_id = override_settings(SITE_ID=site.id)
        site_id.enable()
        self.addCleanup(site_id.disable)

    def user(self, email, syndicate, password=None):
        user = User.objects.create(email=email, username=f'{email}_{syndicate.id}', syndicate=syndicate)
        if password:
            user.set_password(password)
        else:
            user.set_unusable_password()
        user.save()
        return user

    def test_finds_both_records_in_one_syndicate_only(self):
        no_rows = self.user('a@example.com', self.base)  # User.email only
        second = self.user('b@example.com', self.base)
        EmailAddress.objects.create(user=second, email='b2@example.com')
        elsewhere = self.user('a@example.com', self.other)
        self.assertEqual(filter_users_by_email_and_syndicate('A@example.com', self.base), [no_rows])
        self.assertEqual(filter_users_by_email_and_syndicate('b2@example.com', self.base), [second])
        self.assertEqual(filter_users_by_email_and_syndicate('a@example.com', self.other), [elsewhere])

    def reset_form(self, email, **meta):
        request = RequestFactory().post('/', **meta)
        request.user = AnonymousUser()
        return SyndicateSpecificResetPasswordForm(data={'email': email}, request=request)

    def test_password_reset_follows_the_syndicate_header(self):
        user = self.user('y@example.com', self.other, password='REDACTED')
        self.assertFalse(self.reset_form('y@example.com').is_valid())
        form = self.reset_form('y@example.com', HTTP_X_OBICO_SYNDICATE='yumi')
        self.assertTrue(form.is_valid(), form.errors)
        self.assertEqual(form.users, [user])

    def test_password_reset_finds_an_account_without_address_rows(self):
        user = self.user('a@example.com', self.base, password='REDACTED')
        form = self.reset_form('a@example.com')
        self.assertTrue(form.is_valid(), form.errors)
        self.assertEqual(form.users, [user])

from django.contrib.sites.shortcuts import get_current_site
from app.models.syndicate_models import Syndicate
from config.settings import SYNDICATES, SITE_USES_HTTPS
import re

def syndicate_from_request(request):
    # 1. user's account syndicate has the highest priority. But I wouldn't be surprised if we later find edge cases that invalidate this rule.
    if request.user.is_authenticated:
      return request.user.syndicate

    # 2. per-request syndicate comes next.
    syndicate_header = request.META.get('HTTP_X_OBICO_SYNDICATE', None)
    if syndicate_header:
      return Syndicate.objects.get(name=syndicate_header)

    # 3. site syndicate is the default.
    return get_current_site(request).syndicates.first()


def settings_for_syndicate(syndicate_name):
    return SYNDICATES[syndicate_name]


SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE = {}

def build_full_url_for_syndicate(url, syndicate_name):
    global SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE
    if syndicate_name not in SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE:
        SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE[syndicate_name] = Syndicate.objects.get(name=syndicate_name).sites.first().domain

    domain_name = SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE[syndicate_name]

    protocol = 'https://' if SITE_USES_HTTPS else 'http://'
    normalized_url = re.sub(r'^/', '', url)
    return '{}{}/{}'.format(protocol, domain_name, normalized_url)

---
name: jusprin-full-syndicate-decision
description: "2026-11-03: Kenneth chose to make JusPrin a full syndicate with its own accounts, not a branding-only syndicate sharing Obico's account pool."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: c868826d-3950-4f0f-9ecd-4a549cdd6983
  modified: 2026-11-04T17:29:48.875Z
---

2026-11-03 Kenneth's words: "full syndicate with its own accounts." He was choosing between this and a proposal to keep JusPrin accounts in the base Obico pool with JusPrin as a branding-only syndicate (report: side-session-notes/local_cea7b182-1404-4ee3-afa3-e87cbafe7c2d/jusprin-syndicate-one-account-report.md). The report had recommended branding-only; he overruled it.

**Why:** syndicates were designed for branding plus per-brand trickle emails; a separate pool means Obico's trial and drips (which filter on syndicate base) skip JusPrin accounts with no special-casing. This replaces the reverted per-path trial skip (tsd-enterprise 5daee67e1b, reverted by cf01e7adbf).

**How to apply:** an Obico user signing in to JusPrin gets a separate JusPrin account; that is accepted, not a bug. Existing JusPrin v1 users (base-syndicate accounts today; v1 branding comes from a User-Agent check in app/context_processors.py, no syndicate DB row exists): 2026-11-04 Kenneth: "We will tell JusPrin v1 users to re-sign up. We will also manually migrate their subscriptions. The V1 data won't be migrated." So no data-migration code is needed. Related: [[allauth-65-upgrade]].

**2026-11-04 Kenneth picked the host: "jusprin.obico.io"** (staging jusprin-stg.obico.io, my proposal, not his words). Why a host and not the X-Obico-Syndicate header: the app's browser sign-in runs in the system browser, which can't send headers, and an app.obico.io session would authorize /o/authorize/ as the Obico account. Apple sign-in: JusPrin's own sign-in page simply has none (Kenneth). Implemented, committed, not pushed or applied: tsd-enterprise `claude/jusprin-syndicate` (set_up_jusprin_syndicate command, jusprin_subscription_status lists both accounts), JusPrin `claude/elated-sutherland-84a741` 48c7b684f5 (default gateway jusprin.obico.io; v1 import no longer carries v1's token or jusprin_server), ops `claude/jusprin-host` acc4494 (ingress, managed cert, RUNBOOK rollout steps). Local DB has the jusprin syndicate on jusprin.localhost:3334. Test-DB trap: syndicate id sequence starts at 1 beside base's explicit id 1.

content.text:
I took the Obico-account note off JusPrin's own host but kept it where it's still true. The fix is committed in obico-server as 59f41033 on branch `claude/jusprin-login-note`. It's not pushed, so jusprin-stg.obico.io still shows the old note.

**Why I kept the note in one place:** JusPrin v1 opens these same login pages in its built-in browser on app.obico.io. That browser identifies itself as "JusPrin", so the page gets JusPrin branding, but the sign-in still goes to the person's Obico account. For those v1 users the note is still true, so deleting it everywhere would have removed accurate advice. Now both notes appear only when the request signs in to Obico's accounts:
- the login page's "If you have an Obico account, you can use the same account to sign in here";
- the signup page's "do NOT sign up again, use your Obico account", which had the same problem.

On jusprin-stg.obico.io the login page now only says "JusPrin is a project built by Obico."

**What changed:**
- `backend/app/context_processors.py` now gives the page the account pool the request signs in to (`account_syndicate`), next to the branding it already gave.
- `login.html` and `signup.html` check that value.

**Tested against the local stack:**
- I rendered both pages for the JusPrin host and for Obico's host, with and without JusPrin v1's browser identity. Only JusPrin's host changed: the notes are gone there and unchanged everywhere else.
- A new test covers both cases. It passes with the change and fails on master's code.
- The other 43 obico-server app and lib tests pass. The Google sign-in provider's tests can't load in the container because `pytest` isn't installed, with or without my change.

**To get it onto staging:** the branch needs pushing and merging into obico-server, and tsd-enterprise's submodule pointer has to be moved before the next staging release. I didn't touch the submodule pointer.

The code is in a separate copy at `/Users/kenneth/Projects/obico-server-worktrees/jusprin-login-note`, so the branch checked out in your main tsd-enterprise folder is untouched.

content.text:
No, I didn't change how JusPrin v1 behaves on the server, and nothing migrates any v1 data. You decided v1 users will sign up again, you'll move their subscriptions by hand, and v1 data stays where it is. Nothing I built contradicts that.

**Why v1 came up in the last change.** The note I fixed lives on the same login and signup pages that JusPrin v1 opens in its built-in browser on app.obico.io. v1 gets the JusPrin look on those pages from an existing check on the browser's name, but it signs in to Obico accounts. For v1 users, "use your Obico account" is still true. If I had deleted the sentence, I would have changed what v1 users see. So I kept it for that case and only removed it on jusprin-stg.obico.io. I checked both before and after the change: v1's pages are identical, and only the JusPrin host lost the note.

**Other places v1 is touched, none of which migrates anything:**
- **Server, tsd-enterprise:** the `jusprin_subscription_status` command now lists both accounts for an email address, the Obico one (which is where a v1 user's subscription lives) and the new JusPrin one. It only reads. It's there so that when you move a v1 subscription by hand, you can see which account to move it from and to.
- **Desktop app, not the server:** in the JusPrin v2 branch, the import of a v1 user's settings no longer copies v1's sign-in token or v1's server address. So a v1 user who upgrades starts signed out and has to sign up again, as you decided. Their other v1 settings still carry over as before.

(`app-stg.*` to `tsdws-stg-svc`; `app.obico.io`, `app.thespaghettidetective.com`
and `app.kingroon.com` to `tsdws-prod-svc`). The gateway shipped in the normal
release `obi.4048` (2026-10-25), so `stg/update-version.sh` covers both
environments again.

**JusPrin's host: `jusprin.obico.io` (staging `jusprin-stg.obico.io`).**
Decided 2026-11-04. JusPrin is a syndicate of its own, with its own accounts,
and the server takes a request's syndicate from its host. The desktop app's
browser sign-in runs in the system browser, which cannot send the
`X-Obico-Syndicate` header, so only a host of its own keeps JusPrin sign-ins
apart from Obico's. A separate host also gets its own login cookie (the server
sets no cookie domain), so an Obico website session cannot authorize JusPrin.
Rolling it out, staging first:

1. DNS (Namecheap, obico.io): A records `jusprin-stg` and `jusprin` to the
   ingress's static IP, the one `app-stg.obico.io` and `app.obico.io` resolve
   to.
2. `kubectl apply -f tsd/gcp/jusprin-managed-cert.yaml`, then
   `kubectl apply -f tsd/gcp/neg-ingress.yaml` (the ingress names the
   certificate, so the certificate goes first). A certificate is issued once
   its name resolves to the ingress. Staging is in the files now; for
   production add `gke-managed-cert-jusprin-app` for `jusprin.obico.io`, its
   name in the ingress annotation, and a `jusprin.obico.io` rule copied from
   `app.obico.io`'s.
3. On the server, first move the syndicate id sequence past the existing
   rows: base and kingroon were inserted with explicit ids, so on 2026-11-04
   staging's next id was 2 (kingroon's) and production's 1 (base's). In
   `python manage.py shell` on a web pod:
   `from django.core.management.color import no_style; from django.db import connection; from app.models import Syndicate; [connection.cursor().execute(s) for s in connection.ops.sequence_reset_sql(no_style(), [Syndicate])]`
   (done on staging 2026-11-04). Without it the next step fails and rolls
   back. Then:
   `run_django_mgmt_cmd.sh set_up_jusprin_syndicate jusprin-stg.obico.io --google-from app-stg.obico.io`
   (production: `jusprin.obico.io --google-from app.obico.io`). It makes the
   `jusprin` syndicate and the site for the host, takes the site out of the
   base syndicate that a new site joins automatically, and puts Obico's Google
   sign-in app on it. Safe to run again.
4. Google Cloud console, the OAuth client of that Google sign-in app: add
   `https://<host>/accounts/google/login/callback/` as a redirect URI.
5. The desktop app's default gateway (`ProviderProfile.hpp` in JusPrin, the
   "jusprin" row) is `https://jusprin.obico.io/ent/jusprin/v2/responses`. To
   test against staging, set `jusprin_server/base_url` to
   `https://jusprin-stg.obico.io` in the app's settings file.

JusPrin v1 users signed in with Obico accounts on `app.obico.io`. The v1 import
leaves that sign-in behind, they sign up again on JusPrin's host, and their
v1 subscriptions are moved to the new accounts by hand
(`jusprin_subscription_status` lists both accounts of an address).

apart from Obico's. A separate host also gets its own login cookie (the server
sets no cookie domain), so an Obico website session cannot authorize JusPrin.
Rolling it out, staging first:

1. DNS (Namecheap, obico.io): A records `jusprin-stg` and `jusprin` to the
   ingress's static IP, the one `app-stg.obico.io` and `app.obico.io` resolve
   to.
2. `kubectl apply -f tsd/gcp/jusprin-managed-cert.yaml`, then
   `kubectl apply -f tsd/gcp/neg-ingress.yaml` (the ingress names the
   certificate, so the certificate goes first). A certificate is issued once
   its name resolves to the ingress. Staging is in the files now; for
   production add `gke-managed-cert-jusprin-app` for `jusprin.obico.io`, its
   name in the ingress annotation, and a `jusprin.obico.io` rule copied from
   `app.obico.io`'s.
3. On the server, first move the syndicate id sequence past the existing
   rows: base and kingroon were inserted with explicit ids, so on 2026-11-04
   staging's next id was 2 (kingroon's) and production's 1 (base's). In
   `python manage.py shell` on a web pod:
   `from django.core.management.color import no_style; from django.db import connection; from app.models import Syndicate; [connection.cursor().execute(s) for s in connection.ops.sequence_reset_sql(no_style(), [Syndicate])]`
   (done on staging 2026-11-04). Without it the next step fails and rolls
   back. Then:
   `run_django_mgmt_cmd.sh set_up_jusprin_syndicate jusprin-stg.obico.io --google-from app-stg.obico.io`
   (production: `jusprin.obico.io --google-from app.obico.io`). It makes the
   `jusprin` syndicate and the site for the host, takes the site out of the
   base syndicate that a new site joins automatically, and puts Obico's Google
   sign-in app on it. Safe to run again.
4. Google Cloud console, the OAuth client of that Google sign-in app: add
   `https://<host>/accounts/google/login/callback/` as a redirect URI.
5. The desktop app's default gateway (`ProviderProfile.hpp` in JusPrin, the
   "jusprin" row) is `https://jusprin.obico.io/ent/jusprin/v2/responses`. To
   test against staging, set `jusprin_server/base_url` to
   `https://jusprin-stg.obico.io` in the app's settings file.

JusPrin v1 users signed in with Obico accounts on `app.obico.io`. The v1 import
leaves that sign-in behind, they sign up again on JusPrin's host, and their
v1 subscriptions are moved to the new accounts by hand
(`jusprin_subscription_status` lists both accounts of an address).

content.text:
I removed the obico-server change and moved JusPrin's hosts to jusprinv2.obico.io and jusprinv2-stg.obico.io. Staging won't load at its new address until I add its DNS record, and Namecheap needs you to sign in again for that.

**Removed:** the obico-server change had never been pushed, so I deleted its branch. obico-server is back to exactly what it was.

**Renamed to jusprinv2-stg.obico.io:**
- The staging server's database: the JusPrin site's address is now jusprinv2-stg.obico.io. It's still JusPrin's site and still has Google sign-in.
- Ingress and certificate on the cluster: the host rule and a new certificate are for jusprinv2-stg.obico.io, and the old jusprin-stg certificate is deleted. Before applying, I checked that the live ingress differed from the file only by this rename.
- Google sign-in: the redirect address in the Obico OAuth client is now `https://jusprinv2-stg.obico.io/accounts/google/login/callback/`. I reloaded the page to confirm it saved.
- The JusPrin desktop app now signs in to `https://jusprinv2.obico.io`. The two Agent page tests pass. The C++ test changed only its example address and wasn't run.
- The ops runbook and the server setup command's help text use the new names.

None of these are pushed. The ops commit is c0f2b61, JusPrin is a5b10e2f01, and tsd-enterprise is 6a3d8172aa.

**Still to do once you're signed in to Namecheap:** add an A record `jusprinv2-stg` pointing to `34.95.90.112` and delete the old `jusprin-stg` record. Then the new certificate needs time to be issued; last time that took somewhere between 15 minutes and an hour after DNS started working.

**Does obico-server still need a change?** Yes, if the wrong sentence on the JusPrin login page should go away. Renaming the host doesn't remove it. The page shows "If you have an Obico account, you can use the same account to sign in here" whenever the page is in the JusPrin brand, whatever its address. So jusprinv2-stg.obico.io will show it, and anyone who follows it ends up with a new, empty JusPrin account.

Decision needed: should the wrong "use your Obico account" sentence stay on JusPrin v2's server login and signup pages? This is your call because it's what new JusPrin users read and whether obico-server changes at all. Option one: leave obico-server alone and live with the sentence until JusPrin's own sign-in page replaces these server pages. This costs nothing now, but people who sign in with a browser get misled until then. Option two: change obico-server so the sentence shows only where it's still true, JusPrin v1 on app.obico.io. That's the change I just removed: about five lines plus a test, and it leaves v1's pages unchanged. Option three: delete the sentence everywhere. That's a one-line change, but v1 users lose a sentence that's true for them. I'd pick option two, but if JusPrin's own sign-in page is coming soon, option one is reasonable. Which do you want?
